title: U.S. House · Massachusetts's 3rd District
area: Northeastern/Merrimack Valley Massachusetts, including Lowell and Lawrence

context.text: Incumbent Lori Trahan advanced from the September 1, 2026 Democratic primary unopposed. Gary Grossi is the Republican nominee. Dennis Conlon is running as an Unenrolled (independent) candidate after collecting over 2,200 signatures himself.

summary.text: Trahan is the incumbent, serving since 2019. A Lowell native and Georgetown graduate, she worked for Rep. Marty Meehan, rising to chief of staff, before a private-sector career as a tech-company executive and consulting-firm co-founder. First elected in 2018, she sits on the House Energy and Commerce Committee and holds House Democratic leadership roles.

background.text: Born in Lowell, Massachusetts, in 1973; according to her official biography, she is the granddaughter of immigrants and grew up in a working-class family, her father a union ironworker.

Graduated from Lowell Public Schools and Lowell High School, then attended Georgetown University on a volleyball scholarship, according to her official biography; she earned a bachelor's degree in regional and comparative studies in 1995 and says she was the first in her family to graduate from college.
After college joined the staff of then-Rep. Marty Meehan (D), rising to chief of staff.

Spent about a decade in public service before moving to the private sector as an executive at an early-stage tech firm, then co-founded a women-owned consulting firm and served as CEO of the Concire Leadership Institute.
Ran for Congress in 2018, her first campaign for public office, and took office in January 2019.

Serves on the House Energy and Commerce Committee and, in House Democratic leadership, as Co-Chair of the Democratic Policy and Communications Committee, Senior Whip, and a member of the Democratic Steering and Policy Committee, per her official biography.
Her office credits her with securing passage of the Leonel Rondon Pipeline Safety Act after the Merrimack Valley gas explosions and with co-founding the Pandemic Preparedness Caucus.
According to her official biography, she lives in the district with her husband, Dave, and their two daughters.

priorities.text: Lists key issues including addressing racial injustice, the opioid crisis, climate change, education, gun reform, healthcare, immigration, and women's rights on her official issues page.

positions.summary: Official site press material describes her opposing Republican health-care cuts, including on Medicaid.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Energy and Commerce, including its Commerce, Manufacturing, and Trade and Health subcommittees, for 2025-2026.

candidates.name: Gary Grossi

summary.text: Grossi is a nurse and retired U.S. Army colonel running as the Republican nominee. According to his campaign website, he grew up in a Cambridge public housing project, served 29 years in the Army and Army Reserve including a deployment to Iraq, and worked as a nurse at VA medical centers. His campaign website lists affordability, public safety, government transparency and term limits among his priorities.

background.text: Born and raised in Cambridge, Massachusetts, in the Corcoran Park housing project, and graduated from Cambridge High and Latin in 1977, according to his campaign website.
Before nursing school, managed restaurants in Harvard Square and worked in mental health at Metropolitan State Hospital, according to his campaign website.
Earned a bachelor's degree in nursing from UMass Boston.

Served 29 years in the U.S. Army and Army Reserve, according to his campaign website, including as clinical team leader at Walter Reed Army Medical Center, mobilization officer with combat support hospital units, a 2006-2007 deployment to Mosul and Al Asad, Iraq, and Deputy Commander for Nursing Services (colonel) of the 399th Combat Support Hospital from 2007 to 2019.

Worked as a psychiatric nurse at the West Palm Beach VA Medical Center (1995-2000) and in outpatient substance-abuse and psychiatry at the Bedford VA Hospital (2000-2022), and also did community-based substance-abuse and psychiatric care at Choate Hospital in Woburn, per his campaign website.
Received write-in votes in the 2024 Republican primary for the Massachusetts House of Representatives 37th Middlesex District; no candidate advanced from that primary.
Lists himself as vice chair of the Acton Republican Town Committee and a board member of Iron Works Farm, and says he is married with two children, according to his campaign website.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website statements or Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey responses found beyond biographical details.

summary.text: Conlon is a retired analytical chemist and former product-development principal scientist running as an Unenrolled candidate. He says his campaign is self-funded and takes no outside contributions, and that he collected over 2,200 signatures himself to qualify for the ballot. He describes himself as 73 and says he would be content with one term.

background.text: Describes a 43.5-year career as an analytical chemist, most recently as a principal scientist in product development for a medical device manufacturer, and says he holds 9 U.S. patents as an inventor.

BallotReady lists his work history as senior scientist at Bayer Diagnostics (1976-1999), principal scientist at Instrumentation Laboratory (1999-2019), and QC laboratory technician at Cytiva (2021-2022).
BallotReady lists an MBA from Providence College (1993) and a certificate in biopharmaceutical engineering from the University of Massachusetts Lowell (2007).
In his Ballotpedia survey responses, says he has been married 45 years.

priorities.text: "My way is also Finance-Free: I am not taking any money from anyone or any organization ever. Money corrupts politics."
"I am a conservative independent who wants single payer, universal, medicaid for all, whatever you want to call it. ... healthcare is a human right."

positions.summary: Says he supports a single-payer, universal health-coverage system.
positions.quote: I am a conservative independent who wants single payer, universal, medicaid for all, whatever you want to call it.
